---
title: "Setup"
subtitle: "Three platforms, brought online in stages"
---

You will work across **three computing platforms** this quarter. Each has a self-paced tutorial that opens in your browser and ends with a completion checklist. You do not need all three at once: only Tutorial 1 is required before the first class.

| # | Tutorial | Platform | When | What you'll be able to do |
|---|----------|----------|------|---------------------------|
| 1 | [Your Computer: Shell & Git/GitHub](tutorials/01-your-computer.html) | Your laptop/desktop | **Before Week 1** (~1.5 hours) | Install the tools (Git, R, RStudio) and the UW VPN, create your repository from the template, run the clone → commit → push loop |
| 2 | [Raven: RStudio Server & Reproducible Analysis](tutorials/02-raven.html) | Raven | **Week 1**, Thursday session (~1 hour) | Log into the lab server, run an analysis, render a notebook entry, push results |
| 3 | [Hyak / Klone: RStudio on the Cluster](tutorials/03-hyak.html) | Hyak / Klone | **Week 3** (~1 hour) | Launch RStudio on a Klone compute node through OnDemand and run the lab's tools |

::: {.callout-tip}
Raven is home. Your laptop is for editing and Git. Hyak is for when Raven is not enough. Hyak is the hardest of the three; give yourself time and don't panic when something breaks.
:::

## Working off campus

Raven and Hyak OnDemand only load from the UW network. Off campus, connect to **Husky OnNet**, the UW VPN, first. Install it once in [Tutorial 1, Step 6](tutorials/01-your-computer.html#vpn).

## Working in RStudio

On every platform, open your repository as an **R Project** (`fish546.Rproj`) before you start work. It sets the working directory, shows the Git tab, and keeps paths the same on your laptop, Raven, and Klone. See [R Projects in RStudio](r-projects.qmd).

## When you finish a tutorial

Each tutorial ends with a completion block. Paste it as a **comment on your Project Proposal issue** in the [course repository](https://github.com/sr320/course-fish546-2026/issues). That issue is your home base for the quarter; see [How We Work](how-we-work.qmd).

If you have not opened a Project Proposal issue yet, open one first. A rough draft is fine.

## Why these three, and where they come from

Each tutorial maps to the **[Roberts Lab Handbook](https://robertslab.github.io/resources/)**, the reference standard for how you're expected to work:

- **Tutorial 1** → [Computing Best Practices](https://robertslab.github.io/resources/Computing-Best-Practices/), [Data Management](https://robertslab.github.io/resources/Data-Management/), and the handbook's Git/GitHub and bash tutorials.
- **Tutorial 2** → the handbook's Raven (RStudio Server, Conda) guides.
- **Tutorial 3** → UW's [Hyak OnDemand](https://hyak.uw.edu/docs/guides/ood/getting-started) guides and the handbook's Klone guides (containers, file transfers, storage).

Keep the handbook open in a tab while you work — it's where you'll return all quarter.
